text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 2 in history:
1566 - Nostradamus (Michel de Notre-Dame), French physician and astrologer, died.
1644 - The Battle of Marston Moor near York brought the first major Royalist defeat in the English Civil War.
1714 - Christoph Willibald Gluck, German composer of operas including "Orfeo ed Euridice" and "Alceste", born.
1778 - Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Swiss-born French philosopher, died insane. He introduced the concept of "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity".
1819 - The Factory Act was passed in Britain, prohibiting employment of children under nine in textile factories, and children under 16 could only work for 12 hours a day.
1821 - Sir Charles Tupper, Canadian statesman and prime minister in 1896, born. Responsible for legislation making Nova Scotia a province of Canada in 1867.
1850 - Sir Robert Peel, British prime minister (1834-46) and founder of the police force, died as a result of a riding accident.
1853 - The Russian army crossed the Pruth River, invading Turkey and beginning the Crimean War.
1881 - James Garfield, 20th president of the United States, was shot in Washington. He died in September.
1900 - Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin flew his first airship in Germany.
1903 - Sir Alec Douglas-Home, British Conservative prime minister (1963-64), born.
1903 - King Olaf V of Norway born at Sandringham, England. King in 1957, he succeeded his father, King Haakon VII.
1915 - Porfirio Diaz, Mexican soldier and president (1877-1911), died in Paris.
1929 - Imelda Marcos, former Philippine first lady, born. She was toppled from power along with her husband Ferdinand Marcos in 1986.
1932 - King Manuel II of Portugal died. During his reign, he brought an end to the dictatorship of Joao Franco and restored the constitutional monarchy.
1937 - Amelia Earhart and co-pilot Fred Noonan disappeared over the Pacific while trying to fly around the world.
1940 - The liner Arandora Star was torpedoed by a German submarine while transporting German and Italian prisoners to Canada; over 750 prisoners and crew died.
1940 - Adolf Hitler ordered plans to be drawn up for a possible invasion of England.
1961 - Ernest Hemingway, U.S. novelist best known for "A Farewell to Arms" and "For Whom the Bell Tolls", shot himself.
1964 - U.S. President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, prohibiting racial discrimination.
1973 - Betty Grable, U.S. actress, singer and World War Two pin-up girl, died; her films include "How To Marry A Millionaire", "Down Argentine Way" and "Tin Pan Alley".
1976 - North and South Vietnam were reunited as one country with Hanoi as the capital following Vietnam War. It had been divided since 1954.
1985 - Andrei Gromyko became president of the Soviet Union, with Eduard Shevardnadze replacing him as foreign minister. Gromyko died on the same day four years later.
1990 - Over 1,000 Moslem pilgrims died in a stampede in a tunnel at the annual Haj pilgrimage to Mecca.
1994 - An Albanian court sentenced former Communist president Ramiz Alia to nine years jail for abuse of power and violation of citizens' rights.
